P1.evidence: Setter contact acknowledged rather than read back: 'I know you spoke with Kim, he gave me like a little bit of a background so I've got a little bit of a head start anyway.' The prospect had prepared notes and led himself, so nothing was lost, but the 'feel seen' move did not happen. Frame two-part as on every call in this batch — 'get a good idea of where you're at... get a good idea of what it is that you want to achieve' — with no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement token 'Alrighty?' / 'Sure.' Open question run verbatim.

P2.evidence: Age, height, weight and occupation were all volunteered inside the prospect's opening monologue and never asked — 'I'm 5'11", 180 pounds', 'I'm 57', 'my background is I'm a physician'. Hereditary health was volunteered too ('if I look at my dad, I look at my brothers, we've got visceral fat'). The injury is a partial rather than a miss because although the prospect raised it himself with 'sorry, Harry, one more thing', the rep followed up properly: 'How is it when you do push-ups? Is it an issue though?' — and he did claim to have been about to ask. Training week and diet were both properly elicited and in unusual detail. Sleep and energy again absent.

P3.evidence: The six-month success question ran well — 'if we were to fast forward six months, like what is success?' — and both reflect-backs landed and were confirmed: 'It's about recomposition, essentially' and 'It's a lifestyle shift... essentially is what you're looking for.' But the ladder from what to why never started. No bridge question, no 'who else does that impact', no drive to family, legacy or identity. This is a 57-year-old physician with grown children, a family history of visceral fat and a father he compares himself to, and the deepest the call got was 'health is number one for me' — which the prospect said, unprompted, and the rep did not pull on.

P4.evidence: 'I guess what caused you to feel like you want some direction?' is a good adjacent question and produced the history — a previous online cycling coach, plus the flood of contradictory free content ('right now, I'm being fed a million of these, like, well, if you just do this and this for 12 minutes'). The prospect named his own gap unprompted: 'If I know that I have to do something, if I know that I've got a specific workout, that can be a motivator for me.' Nobody asked why the earlier attempts stopped, what the one thing in the way is, or the root-cause question. The obvious answer — a shoulder that hurts every time he restarts — was sitting in the transcript and was never named as the root cause.

P5.evidence: Absent. The prospect supplied every ingredient — a family pattern of visceral fat, an age of 57, 'I just know that 20% body fat's not healthy', a repeating cycle of restart-and-stop — and none of it was converted into a cost of inaction. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no line in the sand. When the money objection arrived at 00:33 there was no consequence frame behind it to push against, which is why the rep had to improvise a comfort-zone argument from scratch.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran properly and, unusually for this batch, before the price: 'Do you feel fully confident that if you had everything that I went through... that we can actually get you to where you want to be? Because that's the most important thing, right?' The all-in question was consciously skipped and the rep said so out loud: 'if you feel like you're ready, I can hear the commitment in your voice. So I don't feel like I need to check you on that.' And the answer he did get was 'I think so' — not the clear YES the playbook requires before moving on, yet he moved on.

P11.evidence: No programme payment. A $100 refundable deposit was collected on the call via a Zoom-chat link, with a receipt confirmed — real but not the step. The onboarding call with Trevor was described ('probably Tuesday or Wednesday') and never booked; what was booked was another sales call. No agreement email, nothing signed, no welcome email, no Skool link, no questionnaire. The calendar invite for the follow-up itself failed to send during the call, which the rep attributed to 'a new software'.

objection_plays.detail: The best-run play in the batch so far. Four moves landed in roughly the scripted order: belief isolate ('Money aside, do you actually feel confident that if you did do it, you would get the results?'), worth test ('Would the results be worth the number?'), the blocker question almost verbatim ('So when it comes to doing your consideration, what specifically is coming up? Is it a logistics thing?'), and the all-in check ('is it a case where this is something that I'm going to do, I just need to get the money? Or is there still a little bit of a concern in between?'). It produced a real diagnosis — a tax bill — rather than a stall. What did not run were the three identity moves: 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', and 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?'. Ends in a deposit, not a decision.

Isolate ran ('Money aside...'), the HOW-not-SHOULD frame ran in paraphrase ('the last thing we want is that money be the thing that holds them back'), and the break-it-up option was offered and a preference confirmed ('which one would you be leaning towards, the in-full or the split?' → 'Oh, the split'). Every one of the six FINANCIAL PICTURE questions was skipped — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments — and the rep never asked permission for the open financial conversation. With a physician who had just volunteered 'I made too much, so I had to pay a lot' in tax, that block would have resolved the objection on the call.

Correctly identified, nearly verbatim: 'Yeah, you're looking for certainty, essentially' — and the prospect confirmed it himself later ('You're right. It's certainty. That's what it is.'). But of the scripted moves only the naming ran. No pleasure-versus-pain question, no BRIDGE, no PLANE, no BURNED BEFORE, no 'how will you know if you never actually try'. The rep substituted his own comfort-zone material and a life-savings-on-a-mentor story, which was well received but is off-script and unrepeatable by another rep.

Timing was the stated blocker — Canadian tax season and a large bill just paid. A single OD-shaped move appeared, garbled in the transcript ('the way I see it is that, you know, it's going to be a big cliff today and next week'). None of the durable OD moves ran: no 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time?', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled'.
No spouse or third-party gate was raised. Family appeared only as a logistics constraint around dinners.

The script gap the playbook already logs. The prospect raised a clinical programme-fit objection in substance — a shoulder that will not tolerate overhead pressing and surgery booked for November, with his own stated intention to 'put it on hold until this got better'. There is no scripted play for this. The rep improvised in the opposite direction to the prospect's own plan, selling the six months as a prehab runway and offering to correct the scapular imbalance, without a single question about clinical clearance. This is where a screening step belongs in the script and there is not one.

notes: Genuinely the strongest objection handling in the batch — the belief check ran before price, the OA diagnosis found the real blocker, and a deposit held the follow-up — sitting on top of a discovery that never asked why any of it mattered and a clinical response that inverted the prospect's own plan for his shoulder. Coach two things: run Phase 5 so the challenge at minute 38 has something to push against, and treat 'I have surgery booked' as a stop-and-screen, not as a reason the six-month term is a good fit.
